text:
Real Estate Moguls Alexander Brothers Face Sexual Abuse Allegations – Survivors Encouraged to Seek Legal Counsel By: Press Advantage March 19, 2025 at 19:04 PM EDT New York, NY – In a significant legal development, real estate moguls the Alexander Brothers are facing serious allegations of sexual abuse, raising concerns about abuse of power in high-profile industries. The case underscores the barriers survivors face when seeking justice, particularly when the accused are individuals of wealth and influence. These allegations highlight the ongoing need to hold perpetrators accountable, no matter their financial status or social standing.
As the allegations unfold, Survivors of Abuse NY , led by Thomas Giuffra, Esq. – The Abuse Lawyer NY, is offering legal guidance and support to any individuals affected. Survivors of sexual abuse in professional settings are encouraged to come forward and explore their legal rights in holding perpetrators accountable. Survivors who have experienced abuse at the hands of powerful individuals should know that legal action may still be possible, despite recent changes to New York’s lookback windows for sexual abuse claims.
New York has made significant strides in providing legal avenues for survivors of sexual abuse . However, some lookback windows have closed, making it critical for survivors to understand their options. The Adult Survivors Act (ASA) previously allowed survivors of sexual offenses that occurred when they were over 18 to file civil lawsuits beyond the statute of limitations. The lookback window closed on November 24, 2023. The Gender-Motivated Violence Act (GMVA) remains open until February 28, 2025, providing survivors of gender-based violence, including coercion, intimidation, or physical force, the opportunity to file a civil lawsuit against their abuser or a complicit institution. The Child Victims Act (CVA), which allowed survivors of childhood sexual abuse to file claims beyond the standard statute of limitations, has also closed.
While some legal deadlines have passed, survivors should consult with an experienced attorney to determine if their case qualifies under existing legal frameworks. Every case is unique, and legal options may still be available depending on the nature of the abuse and when it occurred. Survivors who believe they were subjected to sexual violence that falls under the GMVA should consider taking action before the lookback window closes in early 2025.
Thomas Giuffra, Esq. has spent decades fighting for survivors of sexual abuse, particularly those harmed by powerful individuals and institutions. His firm, Survivors of Abuse NY, provides aggressive legal representation to hold perpetrators and enablers accountable. These cases often involve complex legal challenges, especially when the accused have extensive resources to fight claims. Having a dedicated attorney ensures survivors have the legal support needed to overcome these obstacles.
“Sexual abuse cases involving wealthy and influential figures are often covered up, and survivors are intimidated into silence,” said Thomas Giuffra, Esq. “No one, regardless of their financial or professional status, is above the law. Our NY sexual abuse law firm is committed to ensuring that survivors have the resources, representation, and legal protection they deserve.”
Survivors who pursue civil litigation may be eligible for financial compensation covering therapy and mental health treatment, emotional distress and trauma-related damages, and lost wages and professional setbacks caused by the abuse. Beyond monetary compensation, civil cases expose systemic failures and demand institutional accountability, ensuring that future abuses are prevented.
